causal_defects.evidence: v6 requires a future binding to name claim_generation before its own atomic gpu_pool claim, then rejects the newly generated claimed_at unless it equals that unknowable value.
causal_defects.repair: derive and persist the generation from the successful atomic claim result; future bindings must use an explicit from_atomic_claim mode rather than a timestamp value.

causal_defects.evidence: v6 inspects generation before release but invokes gpu_pool release without --bench and --expected-claimed-at.
causal_defects.repair: release the exact bench with --expected-claimed-at set to the generation captured from the atomic claim.

causal_defects.evidence: v6 publishes repair-ready after the first expected health miss immediately after container launch, instead of supervising normal model load.
causal_defects.repair: wait within a bounded readiness envelope while the exact container remains live; fail early on container exit or fatal log, and publish a fresh-generation repair only on observed failure or readiness deadline.

causal_defects.evidence: v6 SSH, SCP, Docker, repair, and endpoint child calls are not all bounded by the same absolute release deadline.
causal_defects.repair: derive every blocking operation timeout from the smaller of its operation budget and remaining release time; include transfer, remote command, server readiness, repair callback, endpoint, retrieval, and release.

causal_defects.evidence: v6 reuses the fixed fresh-server repair ID after a completed request.
causal_defects.repair: allocate a distinct monotonically increasing repair ID for each server or endpoint repair generation and retain predecessor identity.

timeout fixture proves every blocking child is bounded by remaining release time
second server repair uses a fresh repair ID
